summary:
Summary

STAR HEALTH is an autonomous astronaut health and crisis-monitoring platform for deep-space missions. I developed a decision-support system that runs entirely offline: face-recognition login feeds a zero-latency smart rule engine that analyzes neuro-signals and biometrics against space-medicine reference ranges within milliseconds — no external AI server, no waiting for Earth.

It addresses the challenge of communication delay: on a Mars-class mission, ground approval takes 20–40 minutes, so the platform cross-analyses indicators (e.g., dropping sleep quality + rising Theta waves → micro-sleep / EVA abort warning), scans flight worthiness in seconds, and offers stock-aware recommendations — including non-pharmacological alternatives when supplies are exhausted. It also includes a latency & crisis simulator (ISS / Moon / Mars modes), 3D neuro topography, EEG activity, biometric and radiation monitoring, and a full mission timeline.

It matters because crews are not physicians, and in deep space the ability to decide safely, autonomously and auditably — within milliseconds — is the difference between a managed incident and a lost crew member.
details:
STAR HEALTH

Project Subject: Autonomous Astronaut Health & Crisis Monitoring Software

Project Purpose: To offer a health assistant that tracks astronauts' instant health status and generates its own life-saving solutions on its own — working without internet or an external AI server, even when there is communication delay with Earth during deep-space missions.

Project Overview:

Astronauts are under intense stress, isolation and life-threatening danger because of their work. In microgravity, cosmic radiation and severe sleep deprivation, neurological disorders begin; reaction time, focus and decision-making ability wear down quickly. Besides, not every crew member is a physician, and on distant missions like Mars, waiting for medical approval from Earth can take 20–40 minutes.

That is exactly why I developed Star Health.

How Does Star Health Work?

Astronauts first log in through the face recognition system to access their personalized baseline neuro-signals and space-physiology-specific reference ranges. Instead of waiting for an external AI API, an always-running, zero-latency (offline) smart rule engine analyzes the data within milliseconds and activates predefined space-medicine protocols.

Modules Included:

• Health Metrics Dashboard: The main screen showing the astronaut's instant cognitive performance.

  1. Attention
  2. Working Memory
  3. Sleep Quality
  4. Decision Making
  5. Focus Level
  6. Concentration

• 3D Neuro Topography: Instant and visual marking of brain regions affected by stress, fatigue or radiation on the astronaut's 3D model.

• EEG Wave Activity: Live brain-wave frequencies shown with graphs, based on NASA's open-source data, along with predictive indicators such as risk and EVA (spacewalk) readiness.

• Prediction and Risk (Cross Risk Analysis): A system that catches potential risks early by looking at a combination of multiple indicators rather than a single datum. For example; if sleep quality drops while Theta waves in the brain rise, it issues a "Micro-sleep and EVA Abort Risk" warning.

• Smart Prescription and Stock-Based Alternative Engine (Recommended Action): While telling the astronaut the recommended steps as a result of its assessment, the system also checks the spacecraft's current medication and medical supply stock. If the recommended drug is out of stock or expired due to space radiation, it does not leave the astronaut helpless. It presents, step by step, non-pharmacological alternative methods that can be applied with the equipment available on board (such as blue light therapy, cold compress, breathing exercises or resistance band applications — developable solutions).

• EVA (Spacewalk) Flight Worthiness Approval: A fast control mechanism that scans all neurological and biometric data within seconds before the astronaut goes on a spacewalk and gives a "SAFE / RISKY" decision on whether they can go out on the mission.

• Communication Latency and Crisis Simulator: A simulation area where you can switch between ISS (0 s), Moon (2.6 s) and Mars (22 min delay) modes to test emergency scenarios and prove that the software can operate independently of Earth.

• Mission Timeline: Retrospective record of health changes, radiation accumulation and treatments applied during the mission.

• Biometric Monitoring: Tracking of heart rate, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, body temperature and intracranial pressure / ocular change values (SANS) frequently seen in space.

• Mental Health: Regular assessment of stress, sleep disorder and cognitive fatigue caused by long-term isolation.

• Immune System & Radiation Monitoring: Instant measurement of cosmic radiation exposure and monitoring of immune system resistance accordingly.

• Offline Clinical Decision Assistant: Even if the internet connection is lost, an offline assistant that offers a one-click, step-by-step first aid and measurement guide according to the astronaut's current symptoms or low values.
